Now create the capability. Input: full log text. Output: "verdict <holds|violates|error>\ninvariant <Name or ->\ntrace <n>".

Lambda in Common Lisp:

```lisp
(lambda (input)
  (let* ((lines (uiop:split-string input :separator '(#\Newline)))
         (violates (or (search "is violated." input)
                       (search "Temporal properties were violated" input)))
         (holds (search "No error has been found." input))
         (verdict (cond (violates "violates")
                        (holds "holds")
                        (t "error")))
         (invariant (if violates
                        (let ((start (search "Error: Invariant " input)))
                          (if start
                              (let* ((s (+ start (length "Error: Invariant ")))
                                     (e (search " is violated." input :start2 s)))
                                (subseq input s e))
                              "-"))
                        "-"))
         (trace (count-if (lambda (l) (and (>= (length l) 7) (string= (subseq l 0 7) "State ")))
                          lines)))
    (format nil "verdict ~a~%invariant ~a~%trace ~a" verdict invariant trace)))
```

Careful with the "State " prefix — lines begin "State 1: <Initial predicate>". "State " with a space, 6 chars. `(string= (subseq l 0 6) "State ")`. Also note "states generated" lines contain " states generated" not starting with "State ". And "State " at start of line only matches state lines. Also "Finished computing initial states: ..." starts with "Finished", fine. "Error: The behavior up to this point is:" — fine.

Note: the log also contains "State 1: <Initial predicate>" etc. All good.

```lisp
(lambda (input)
  (let ((violates (or (search "is violated." input)
                      (search "Temporal properties were violated" input)))
        (holds (search "No error has been found." input))
        (trace 0))
    (with-input-from-string (s input)
      (loop for line = (read-line s nil)
            while line
            do (when (and (>= (length line) 6)
                          (string= (subseq line 0 6) "State "))
                 (incf trace))))
    (let* ((verdict (cond (violates "violates") (holds "holds") (t "error")))
           (invariant
             (if violates
                 (let ((start (search "Error: Invariant " input)))
                   (if start
                       (let* ((s (+ start (length "Error: Invariant ")))
                              (e (search " is violated." input :start2 s)))
                         (if e (subseq input s e) "-"))
                       "-"))
                 "-")))
      (format nil "verdict ~a~%invariant ~a~%trace ~a" verdict invariant trace))))
```

One catch: "Temporal properties were violated" — check search order: violates takes precedence over holds. If a log had "No error has been found." it wouldn't contain "is violated." anyway.

Also note: `(search " is violated." input :start2 s)` — search's second arg is the sequence to search, and :start2 is the start in that sequence. Correct.

Potential issue: "Error: Invariant " might match something in an error log unrelated... but per rules, only relevant when violates, and the name is from that line. Fine.
